about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Jeff Hurd

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DON YOUNG DOUG LaMALFA INDIAN BUFFALO MANAGEMENT ACT
statements.title: DON YOUNG DOUG LaMALFA INDIAN BUFFALO MANAGEMENT ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in support of my legislation, H.R. 7954, the Don Young Doug LaMalfa Indian Buffalo Management Act.

As chairman of the Natural Resources Subcommittee on Indian and Insular Affairs, one of my priorities has been advancing practical legislation that respects Tribal sovereignty and strengthens Tribal self-determination.
I am also proud that this legislation now carries the names of two Members who cared deeply about Indian Country: Don Young of Alaska and my friend, Doug LaMalfa of California.

I thank the InterTribal Buffalo Council; the Wildlife Conservation Society; the National Bison Association; Chairman Westerman; and the Natural Resources Committee and staff, especially Kirstin Liddell on our Indian and Insular Affairs Subcommittee, for their work to move this legislation forward.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to support this bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FINISH THE ARKANSAS VALLEY CONDUIT ACT--VETO MESSAGE FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES
statements.title: FINISH THE ARKANSAS VALLEY CONDUIT ACT--VETO MESSAGE FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES
sentences: When we talk about honoring Federal commitments, we are talking about whether the people who grow our food can have clean water.
It lets communities doing their part and repaying the government finally access clean water.

On October 3, 2020, President Trump's Department of the Interior issued a press release titled: ``Trump administration breaks ground on long-awaited Arkansas Valley Conduit to bring safe, clean water to rural Colorado communities.'' Earlier that year, the President visited Colorado and praised the Arkansas Valley Conduit.

However, I would ask every Member to consider the pressure felt by the communities they represent, especially those in rural America who need infrastructure built, who need clean water, and who need Washington to mean what it says.
